data.name: DopplerInsights.Subtitle
data.value: Load a pass log to see clear tuning advice for Adaptive threshold and Lead Doppler CAT settings.

data.name: DopplerInsights.Chart.Legend
data.value: Blue = downlink tracking error, Orange = uplink tracking error, Teal band = adaptive threshold zone, Dashed = base threshold, Purple ticks = CAT corrections, Grey strip = satellite elevation, Amber line = TCA (highest elevation)

data.name: DopplerInsights.Chart.Explain
data.value: Each coloured line shows how far the radio frequency drifted from the calculated Doppler target. When error reaches the threshold, OscarWatch sends a CAT correction (purple tick) and error drops back. Smaller, smoother cycles mean better tracking.

data.name: DopplerInsights.Chart.Hint
data.value: Use +/− buttons to zoom, or scroll horizontally to pan

data.name: DopplerInsights.Section.HowTo
data.value: How to use this to tune radio settings

data.name: DopplerInsights.HowTo.Intro
data.value: Use this panel to compare one pass before and after changing settings.

data.name: DopplerInsights.HowTo.Step1
data.value: 1) If "Suppressed by threshold" is very high and RX/TX writes are low, lower Doppler threshold slightly.

data.name: DopplerInsights.HowTo.Step2
data.value: 2) If RX/TX write rates are very high, increase threshold or CAT delay to reduce chatter.

data.name: DopplerInsights.HowTo.Step3
data.value: 3) If peak slew is high and tracking lags, enable/increase Lead Doppler for CAT latency.

data.name: DopplerInsights.HowTo.Step4
data.value: 4) Use compare mode: aim for lower p95 deltas with stable write rates and fewer manual interventions.

data.value: IC-9700 default A2, IC-910 default 7C (hex). Use 60 if your radio is set that way in the CI-V menu.

data.name: Settings.Radio.Ft847Hint
data.value: FT-847: set CAT baud in radio menu #37 (typically 57600). Use the CAT/LINEAR jack with a level converter (e.g. CT-62).

data.name: Settings.Radio.Ts2000Hint
data.value: TS-2000: CAT 57600 8N1. Select SAT on the radio and turn memory mode off before tracking; OscarWatch then enables SATL via CAT (SA/FA/FB layout), auto VHF/UHF band swap.

data.name: Settings.Radio.Ts2000HardwareRtsNote
data.value: Leave on for full CAT cables that pass RTS (required for radio replies). Turn off if your cable or adapter has no hardware flow control.

data.name: Settings.Radio.Ts2000TraceNote
data.value: Leave on for the radio's built-in frequency tracking. Turn off when OscarWatch manages Doppler (recommended for PC CAT tracking); try both if unsure.

data.name: Settings.Radio.RegionNote
data.value: EU uses tone; USA uses tone squelch (subtone).

data.name: Settings.Radio.CatDelayNote
data.value: Minimum time between CAT commands to protect the serial link.

data.name: Settings.Radio.SdrEnterHostPort
data.value: Enter a valid host and port.

data.name: Settings.Radio.SdrConnectionOk
data.value: rigctl connection OK — frequency read succeeded.

data.name: Settings.Radio.SdrHint
data.value: Enable the rigctl server in SDR++ (Module Manager → rigctl_server) or SDR Connect, then match host and port. OscarWatch pushes Doppler RX frequency and reads the waterfall VFO for passband trim. Use 100 ms or more CAT delay on the downlink.

data.name: Settings.Radio.FlexEnterHostPort
data.value: Enter a valid host and port.

data.name: Settings.Radio.FlexDiscoveryListening
data.value: Listening for Flex radios on UDP 4992…

data.name: Settings.Radio.FlexDiscoveryFound

data.name: Settings.Radio.FlexHint
data.value: Pick a discovered radio or enter the IP manually (TCP port 4992). OscarWatch connects directly to the radio over the SmartSDR TCP/IP API (not by automating SmartSDR for Windows), enables full duplex, and drives separate RX/TX slices for Doppler. Use the antenna port map below when transverters use different RX A/RX B or ANT/XVTR paths per band. Dual-SCU models are required for true full duplex (e.g. 8600/8600M; also 6600/6700).

data.name: Settings.Radio.FlexAntennaPortsHint
data.value: When switching U/V ↔ V/U satellites, OscarWatch sets the radio’s RX/TX ports from the downlink and uplink bands (on satellite focus / pass setup — not only when the bird is above the horizon). Leave unchanged keeps the radio’s current port. RX A and RX B are receive-only; map TX to ANT or XVTR as wired.

data.name: Settings.Radio.FlexDuplexWarning
data.value: This model may not support full duplex (single SCU). Satellite use typically needs a dual-SCU Flex such as an 8600/8600M (or a dual-SCU 6000-series radio) with suitable isolation or transverters.

data.name: Settings.Radio.Ic705CivHint
data.value: IC-705 factory default A4. Must match the radio CI-V menu.

data.name: Settings.Radio.Ic7300CivHint
data.value: IC-7300 factory default 94H. Must match the radio CI-V menu.

data.name: Settings.Radio.Ic905CivHint
data.value: IC-905 factory default AC. Must match the radio CI-V Set mode.

data.name: Settings.Radio.Ic706CivHint
data.value: IC-706 factory default 48H. Must match the radio CI-V address (Initial Set Mode).

data.name: Settings.Radio.Ic706MkiiCivHint
data.value: IC-706MKII factory default 4CH. Must match the radio CI-V address.

data.name: Settings.Radio.Ic706MkiiGCivHint
data.value: IC-706MKIIG factory default 58H. Must match menu 34 CI-V ADDRES.

data.name: Settings.Radio.Ft817Hint
data.value: FT-817 / FT-818: Set menu #14 to 4800 baud on each radio (38400 also works). 8N2 CAT — one COM per leg. Covers HF/6 m, 2m, and 70cm (AO-07 Mode A downlink on 10 m). Linear: spin downlink for passband; FM locks dial while tracking.

data.name: Settings.Radio.Ic705Hint
data.value: IC-705: Set Connectors → CI-V → CI-V USB Port to Link to [CI-V] (not REMOTE). Match CI-V baud in Settings (default 115200). One COM port per leg — use the port labelled CI-V when two appear.

data.name: Settings.Radio.Ic7300Hint
data.value: IC-7300: Dual radio only. HF/6 m coverage (1.8–54 MHz). Match CI-V address (default 94H) and baud (default 115200) in the radio CI-V menu. One COM port per leg — typical for AO-07 Mode A with the 7300 on downlink and a 2 m radio on uplink.

data.name: Settings.Radio.Ic905Hint
data.value: IC-905: Dual radio only. Match CI-V address (default AC) and baud (default 115200) in Set mode. Use the USB CI-V serial port. One COM port per leg — covers VHF/UHF/SHF including 13 cm, 6 cm, and 3 cm.

data.name: Settings.Radio.Ic706Hint
data.value: IC-706: CI-V via the REMOTE jack (or CT-17). HF/6 m and 2m (no 70cm). Set CI-V address and baud in Initial Set Mode (LOCK at power-on) to match Settings (default 48H / 19200). CI-V TRN On recommended. AO-07 Mode A downlink on 10 m is supported.

data.name: Settings.Radio.Ic706MkiiHint
data.value: IC-706MKII: same CI-V setup as IC-706. HF/6 m and 2m (no 70cm). Factory default address 4CH. AO-07 Mode A downlink on 10 m is supported.

data.name: Settings.Radio.Ic706MkiiGHint
data.value: IC-706MKIIG: CI-V via the REMOTE jack (or CT-17). Set menu 34 CI-V ADDRES to match Settings (default 58H), menu 35 CI-V BAUD to match Settings (default 19200), and menu 36 CI-V TRN On. Covers HF/6 m, 2m, and 70cm (AO-07 Mode A downlink on 10 m); 23cm satellites are not supported.

data.name: Settings.Radio.Ft991Hint
data.value: FT-991 / FT-991A: Match menu 031 CAT RATE to Settings (default 38400). 8N2 ASCII CAT with hardware RTS — use the USB CAT COM port. One COM per leg. FM locks the VFO-A dial while tracking.

data.name: Settings.Radio.Ftx1Hint
data.value: FTX-1 Field / FTX-1optima: Match menu CAT-1 RATE to Settings (default 38400). 8N2 ASCII CAT with hardware RTS — use the Enhanced COM port (CAT-1), not CAT-2. One COM per leg. FM locks the MAIN VFO dial while tracking.

data.name: Settings.Radio.CwSideband
data.value: Linear CW: keep receive in USB/LSB (transmit CW only)

data.name: Settings.Radio.CwSidebandNote
data.value: Applies when the frequency panel is set to CW on linear SSB satellites. Checked is the usual split (CW TX, USB/LSB RX). Unchecked sets both VFOs to CW.

data.name: Settings.Radio.DopplerFmNote
data.value: FM / ISS cross-band: lower = more CAT updates (default 350 Hz).

data.name: Settings.Radio.DopplerSsbNote
data.value: Frequencies are sent to the radio only when drift exceeds this interval (SatPC32-style).

data.name: Settings.Radio.DialSettleNote
data.value: On linear USB, LSB, and CW, how long the receive dial must stay still before OscarWatch resumes Doppler CAT. Default 800 ms. Increase if CAT takes the VFO back while you are still tuning; decrease if you want tracking back sooner.

data.name: Settings.Radio.UplinkResumeNote
data.value: On Main/Sub radios (for example IC-9700), extra wait before uplink CAT after you stop turning the dial, so the radio does not hop to Sub while you scan. Dual radio is not affected. Default 2500 ms.

data.name: Settings.Radio.DopplerAdaptiveThresholdNote
data.value: When enabled, linear SSB/CW threshold is lowered while Doppler slew is fast (typically mid-pass and post-TCA). Your SSB/CW value above remains the ceiling; effective threshold can drop to about half (minimum 25 Hz). Off by default.

data.name: Settings.Radio.DopplerPassLogNote
data.value: Writes one CSV per pass with CAT writes, 1 s snapshots (lead, adaptive threshold, deltas), and offset/knob changes. Logging runs only while the satellite is above the horizon (elevation ≥ 0°). Saved under AppData/OscarWatch/doppler-logs.

data.name: Settings.Radio.DopplerCatLeadNote
data.value: When enabled, CAT and the Radio row predict Doppler ahead on steep and post-TCA legs (when range rate is changing quickly). Near TCA, lead tapers off as range rate approaches zero. Gentle AOS uses the current rate. The Sat row still shows the current spacecraft frequency. Fine-tune with lead time and strength below.

data.name: Settings.Radio.DopplerCatLeadMsNote
data.value: 0 = automatic (half your CAT delay, capped at 50 ms, or 75 ms post-TCA). Set explicitly to trim how far ahead Doppler is predicted without changing CAT pacing.

data.name: Settings.Radio.DopplerCatLeadGainNote
data.value: 100 = full computed lead. Lower if the radio feels ahead of the signal (try 70–85). Does not affect the Sat row.

data.name: Settings.Rotator.TypeNote
data.value: GS-232 for Yaesu and clones. SPID for controllers in SP mode (Rot1Prog / Rot2Prog). EasyComm for EC mode (SPID, M2, and other text-protocol controllers). SAEBRTrack for classic satellite tracker interfaces (9600 baud). OZ9AAR URC (TCP) for the Ultimate Rotator Controller over Ethernet (default port 1111; set URC to REM/remote mode). Green Heron RT-21 Az-El uses two COM ports (azimuth and elevation), DCU-1 protocol at 4800 baud; do not select GS-232. Serial protocols can also use a TCP serial server (e.g. ser2net) instead of a local COM port.

data.name: Settings.Rotator.DualSerialNote
data.value: The RT-21 Az-El has two USB serial ports (one per axis). Assign azimuth and elevation carefully: swapping them points the wrong motor. On Linux prefer stable by-id paths so the ports do not swap after reboot.

data.name: Settings.Rotator.NetworkNote
data.value: OscarWatch connects as a TCP client. On the URC, enable the socket server and select remote (REM) tracking mode so GOTO commands move the antennas. Default port is 1111.

data.name: Settings.Rotator.NetworkNoteTcpSerial
data.value: OscarWatch connects as a TCP client to a raw serial tunnel (for example ser2net). Configure baud rate and serial options on the server. Best used on a local network — high latency can cause timeouts.

data.name: Settings.Rotator.SmartAzimuthNote
data.value: On 450° rotators (e.g. Yaesu G-5500), commands 361–450° avoid a long slew back through 0° when the pass will cross north. Passes that head north but stay east of 0° remain in the primary band.

data.name: Settings.Rotator.ElevationRangeNote
data.value: 0–90° for standard rotators. 0–180° for over-the-top mounts (e.g. Yaesu G-5500) that can track past zenith.

data.name: Settings.Rotator.KeyholeNote
data.value: When enabled, high-elevation passes where the rotator cannot keep up near zenith are analysed, and the rotator may pre-position in a flipped orientation to minimise signal loss. Only available when elevation range is 0–180°.

data.name: Settings.Rotator.KeyholeSlewRateNote
data.value: Maximum rotator slew rate in degrees per second. Used to compute signal-loss windows.

data.name: Settings.Rotator.KeyholeThresholdNote
data.value: Minimum maximum-elevation for a pass to be classified as entering the keyhole zone. Valid range: 60–89°.

data.name: Settings.Rotator.TrackStartNote
data.value: Default is -3° (below horizon). Range -90° to 90°. The rotator begins slewing when the tracked satellite rises above this elevation, and parks once it drops below (after a short confirm so a single glitch tick cannot interrupt the pass).

data.name: Settings.Rotator.ParkNote
data.value: Park position is used when no satellite is above the tracking threshold. The focused pass or live satellite is tracked automatically. Manual Park on the main window and standby mode are not affected.

data.name: Settings.Rotator.OffsetNote
data.value: Added to pass tracking and manual rotate commands (not park). Use positive values if the beam stops short of the target; negative if it overshoots.

data.name: Settings.Recording.EnableNote
data.value: Records audio from the selected input device while the focused satellite is above the start elevation. Choose WAV or MP3 (MP3 needs ffmpeg on PATH). Files are saved with UTC timestamps.
